title: Locked Doors
story: Two locked doors stand between you and a vault. Each one is jammed by its file permissions. Fix them one by one.
description:
Door 1: ~/doors/door1.txt has a passcode, but you can’t read it. Make it readable.

Door 2: ~/doors/door2.key is too open. Change its permissions so they read exactly rw-r-----.

The Lock: ~/doors/unlock.sh won’t run. Make it runnable, then run it.

The Vault: /opt/vault/flag.txt belongs to root—you need superuser powers to read what's inside it.
hints: Check the current permissions inside `~/doors/` and make `~/doors/door1.txt` readable so you can view its PASSCODE.
Set `~/doors/door2.key` permissions to octal `640` (`rw-r-----`), then make `~/doors/unlock.sh` executable and run it.
Once `~/doors/unlock.sh` unseals the vault, read `/opt/vault/flag.txt` using `sudo` and submit the flag with `quest submit`.
